text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — saw a 3x spike in requeues during a handful of preemptible drains in us-west-2 last night. Almost all failures are streaming requests that were mid-token when eviction hit. Sample log: 
```
ERROR stream_write: lost_kv_cache: missing_prefix, token_seq=1423, node=gpu-112, eviction_signal=SIGTERM
WARN requeue: no_replay_token, request_id=rpc-7c9a
```
Anyone seen similar? thinking this is a cutover / token-stitching race rather than pure queue starvation. :thinking:

Ajay Patel: Yep — that's the token-stitch race. Current cutover swaps routing immediately when node marks draining, but mid-stream sessions lose KV pointers. Quick mitigation: keep the old streaming path alive until a handshake ACK from router confirms router has copied the latest KV checkpoint. We used a similar pattern in prior non-preemptible rollouts.

Liam O'Neill: Concrete flow I propose:
1) On drain, runtime emits a short-lived handoff_token (ttl ~30s) tied to KV snapshot id.
2) Router continues forwarding to old node while issuing that token to new node.
3) New node pulls snapshot via token and replies with `handoff:ack`.
4) Router switches traffic only after ack or after a conservative timeout (e.g., 800ms).
This avoids mid-token blind switches. Also add idempotent replay at sequence level.

Sophie Rivera: Sounds solid. Two operational notes: 1) tail-latency could increase slightly due to the ack wait; we should restrict to preemptible pool only (not on-demand) and keep a low default timeout (500-1000ms). 2) Cost/throughput: if handoff leads to duplicate work spikes, we should fallback to mixing in on-demand capacity for the tail rather than over-provisioning spot.

Maria Chen: Agree. We need metrics to trigger fallback automatically. Proposal:
- metric: `stream_requeue_rate` (1m)
- threshold: >0.8% -> route new streams to mixed-capacity fallback (reserve 10% on-demand)
- threshold: >2% for 5m -> rollback handshake change
Also add a canary: enable handshake only for 5% of preemptible drains in us-west-2 for first 24h.

Ajay Patel: Router config sketch (canary + ack timeout):
```yaml
routing:
  drain_handoff:
    enabled: true
    ack_timeout_ms: 800
    canary_pct: 5
    fallback_policy:
      type: mixed_capacity
      on_demand_pct: 10
```
Keep in mind the validation: ensure `handoff_token` grants limited read-only snapshot access and expires on first use.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout for us-west-2 preemptible pool at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z (canary=5%). CI job `handoff-e2e` queued.

oncall-bot: incident created: #IN-2026-44 for tracking requeue regression alerts during rollout. Pager oncall: @Sophie Rivera.

Liam O'Neill: One more runtime detail — add a tiny in-memory replay buffer (500-1000 tokens) so the new node can request a short tail if it needs to stitch up missing context. That buys us safety without persisting everything.

Sophie Rivera: Ops runbook additions:
- If `stream_requeue_rate` spikes >1% within 10m after canary, pause rollout and promote 20% on-demand fallback.
- If `handoff_latency` (ack wait) >1200ms, lower ack_timeout to 400ms and increase canary sample to collect more short-lived cases.

Maria Chen: OK action items:
- @Ajay implement handoff_token + ack in router (PR + unit tests)
- @Liam add replay buffer + KV snapshot fetch path
- @Sophie add metrics/alert rules and runbook text
- @SRE rotate oncall for the canary window
We'll meet async in #eng-runtime if anything pops. Thanks :thumbsup:
